doc.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Farmingdale High School and Marshall Brown's Newport Youth Band
summary: At Farmingdale High School Marshall Brown's jazz band, tutored by LaPorta and Mucci, led to the Newport Youth Band with Gomez, Cuber, Owens and Rosen; learning how to rehearse a band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Was living in New York — this is probably a yes — a positive place to be for your craft?

Well I was born in Brooklyn, New York and then when I was about I think 12 years old we moved out to Farmingdale, Long Island which is a very important part, because, and the only reason we moved is my sister and her family decided to move and the Italian thing is you know your kids go there, you got to go, you can’t, it’s not like you are oceans away. So we wound up on Long Island of course now what a drag, I’m trying to play. So I was in a school called Farmingdale High School and the band director was a man by the name of Marshall Brown who was probably one of the foremost beginning of the jazz educators along with people like Clem DeRosa and the John LaPortas and others on the east coast we’re talking. And he had a high school band that we had John LaPorta and Lou Mucci who played lead trombone along with Gil Evans and Claude Thornhill, Marshall would get those guys in to tutor the band. And we’d have doctor — he would take some stock arrangements and doctor them up and change them and then we’d have LaPorta would write original stuff for the band. So we are doing jazz festivals and we’re doing all the dances. So the school got bugged because we were getting notoriety as a jazz band. So the bottom line was — there was a combination — Marshall was fired and then he quit. Then he went on to start with George Wein and the Lorillards who were running the Newport Festival, the thing called the Newport Youth Band which was musicians audition from all over the greater area. You had to be a certain age. So basically in that band the drummer was Larry Rosen, the R of GRP Records, Eddie Gomez was the bassist and another wonderful bassist Herbie Moutin is one of the great bass teachers in L.A., Eddie Daniels, Ronnie Cuber a baritone player, myself, Jimmy Owens, a trumpet player. So I mean we had a hell of a band. And we had all the music written for us. Bill Holman, Ernie Wilkins, Quincy, Bill Russo. So we had tons, all this ©Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

original, and I started writing for the band at one point. So it was a wonderful experience, also learning how to rehearse a band too. Again John LaPorta and Lou Mucci would come in and rehearse, tutor the band, in phrasing, so you talk about jazz education, my God. So to this day I feel I have, and Jimmy Owens, we’ve always discussed this, about how to rehearse a band and how to deal with students. We feel we’ve had an advantage you know, kind of making it fun and Marshall was brilliant in the sense that he knew what he could do, but he knew who to hire to do it good. And this is how, I mean Larry Rosen was the same at GRP, he realized he had, he could do a certain thing but he knew who to hire to make his company work. So and that to me is the smarts.
